One syscall per byte, where one per buffer would do
write_all can fail and is never checked
writing.exampleCaption: One syscall per line, versus one per buffer.
writing.explanation: Reading a file, opening a socket, or spawning a thread all cross a privilege boundary that costs far more than a function call. That is why buffered IO exists, why writev beats many writes, and why an event loop with epoll or io_uring outperforms a read per connection. Interviewers ask this to see whether you know where the cost of IO actually is.
writing.feedback: The boundary crossing dominates; batch before you optimise anything else.
